correctness.rationale: On the vacuum-to-one-excitation coherence operators, the independent equal-rate dephasing dissipator is exactly \(-\kappa\) times the identity. The Hamiltonian preserves this sector, so the output coherence equals the noiseless transfer amplitude times \(e^{-\kappa t}\). The normalized Choi partial transpose has a two-by-two block of determinant \(-|c|^2/4\); for a qubit channel this is entangled exactly when \(c\ne 0\). Perfect transfer therefore remains non-entanglement-breaking for every finite rate. The packaged checker independently replays the algebraic sign tests; finite tests are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result converts a finite numerical observation into an exact all-chain-length, all-finite-dephasing theorem and yields a reusable structural criterion based only on the noiseless transition amplitude. It is not a mere recomputation: it exposes an invariant coherence sector even though the full coherent and dissipative superoperators fail to commute, and quantitatively certifies a negative Choi partial-transpose eigenvalue. The limitation that entanglement persistence need not mean useful fidelity is explicit.
